sn1.23:1.1: The “tangle” (_jaṭā_) is the tangled hair or dreadlocks of the Brahmanical _jaṭila_ ascetics, as is made clear in [sn7.6]() where a dreadlocked brahmin opens with the same verse. The claim is that _jaṭila_ ascetics are as tangled in their minds by craving as they are in their hair.
sn1.23:2.1: In a bold literary conceit, the vast compendium of the Visuddhimagga positions itself as an explanation of this single verse.
sn1.23:2.2: Here _citta_ (“mind”) stands for _samādhi_ or _jhāna_, which is normally the case in the Suttas on the path (eg. _cittasampadā_ = _samādhisampadā_, _cittabhāvanā_ = _samādhibhāvanā_, _adhicitta_ = _samādhi_, etc.)
sn1.23:3.1: The previous verse dealt with the one who is practicing; this verse with the perfected one; and the final verse with final extinguishment.
